title: Characteristics of CdTe Solar Cells Irradiated Under Neutron Beam
content: Thin-film CdTe solar cells are a promising option for power generation in space missions due to their low cost, high power-to-weight ratio, and reliability in harsh environments [1-2]. While extensive research has been conducted on the effects of proton and electron radiation on CdTe solar cells, relatively few studies have reported their response to neutron radiation. Such knowledge is vital for deep space exploration, where solar cells may be subjected to significant neutron flux originating from cosmic rays and secondary particle interactions. Here, we investigate the effects of neutron irradiation on CdTe solar cells in a TRIGA (Training, Research, Isotopes, General Atomics) reactor at the University of Utah that provides a high neutron flux (≈ 1012 n/cm2/sec).
